description: Guide the student to fetch historical market price data and macroeconomic data from public APIs using Python, save both datasets as CSV files, and teach quant data-ingestion validity concepts (adjusted prices, macro revisions/release lag, and point-in-time usage). Evaluation in this Track A task is hybrid: tutor output quality plus runnable-code evidence from tool logs.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: I want to practice real quant data work. Can you help me write Python code to download historical market prices and macro data from free APIs, save them to CSV, and explain what data pitfalls I should watch out for?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: I need a clean ingestion script for historical asset prices plus macro indicators using only docs. Also teach me the quant validity checks: adjusted vs raw prices, release lag, revisions, and point-in-time risk.
student_openings.advanced_quant: Let's build a reproducible historical ingestion pipeline from official APIs with schema normalization and CSV persistence, then audit for corporate-action handling and macro point-in-time/revision leakage.

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Tutor provides persona-adapted instruction quality for historical data ingestion, demonstrates runnable code execution, and clearly explains quant caveats: adjusted prices/corporate actions, macro release-lag and revisions, and point-in-time leakage risk.

required_capabilities.description: Adapts explanation depth to learner level
required_capabilities.evidence: beginner receives plain-language scaffolding, intermediate receives implementation-oriented guidance, advanced receives methodology-level caveats

required_capabilities.description: Explains adjusted vs unadjusted prices and corporate-action effects
required_capabilities.evidence: mentions adjusted prices, splits/dividends, and why unadjusted series can distort backtests

required_capabilities.description: Explains macro release lag/revision and point-in-time risk
required_capabilities.evidence: mentions release lag or revisions and warns against using revised/future-known values at trade time
gives concrete checks or checklist the student can run after fetching data
